newsitem.title: UK: Ladbroke signs deals for 12 new hotels.
newsitem.headline: Ladbroke signs deals for 12 new hotels.

text.p: Leisure and gaming group Ladbroke said on Thursday its Hilton International (HIC) subsidiary had signed contracts to operate 12 new hotels in the year to date.

Finance Director Brian Wallace said the company was in line with its aim of having 20 new properties this year. It has agreements in place for a further 30 hotels which will open by the turn of the century.

HIC, acquired by Ladbroke in October 1987, operates almost 160 hotels in some 50 countries worldwide outside the United States. It has just three hotels in the U.S. where Hilton Hotels Corp has exclusive rights to the Hilton brand.
Its hotels are a mixture of owned, leased and managed properties.
Hilton Hotels Corp (HHC) and Ladbroke on Thursday announced an outline agreement on an alliance to reunite the Hilton brand worldwide for the first time since 1964.
As part of the deal, HIC will be responsible for the future development of the Conrad brand outside the United States.
The Conrad brand internationally comprises nine hotels, including a 513-room property in Hong Kong. The plan is to rebrand these nine hotels as Hiltons.
HHC is the sixth largest hotel company in the U.S. and owns, manages and franchises the operation of some 220 properties.
Its top hotels include The Waldorf Astoria in New York, the Washington Hilton and Towers and Chicago's Palmer House Hilton.
Founder Conrad Hilton purchased his first hotel, the Mobley, in the Texan town of Cisco in 1919.
HIC was spun off as a separate company 32 years ago.
